result.summary: The contractor's message in event 009 only confirmed that the quote had been sent, so it didn't need a reply. The quote is in attachment-02: £90 for the requested scope. The earlier landlord approval (event 002) had no amount attached, so I emailed the landlord asking them to approve the £90 cost. I took the ticket out of the vacancy pause and moved it to landlord_approval, then placed a hold with a 2-day follow-up.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 008 asked whether the provider needed a response. Event 009 is a plain confirmation (classify_reply: auto, needs_human_response 0.13), so it did not. The quote (attachment-02) covers exactly the scope in event 001 and the checkout report, for a total of £90. The approval in event 002 was given before any cost was known (approval 50 has no amount), and the landlord has no recorded pre-approved spend limit. A specific £90 cost sign-off is therefore needed before the clean is booked. The 'not tenanted' pause (event 004) is expected for a checkout clean and doesn't block the job.

alternatives_considered.option: Instruct the contractor to proceed at £90 on the strength of the event 002 approval
alternatives_considered.why_not: That approval had no amount and there is no recorded spend limit, so going ahead would commit the landlord's money to a cost they haven't seen.
The pause is only because the property is vacant, which is normal for a checkout clean. Leaving it paused would stall the job.
There is no conflict, safety issue or dispute. Getting a routine cost sign-off from the landlord is the normal next step.
